BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE 01.

Succinctly stated the facts discernible from the present complaint are that complainant was running a spare part shop He was residing in April 2005 at the house bearing no. 1780 Janta Flat,
GTB Enclave which belonged to his father.
It is further stated in the complaint that his father sold the above said property to Chandrakant (PO), S/o Murari Lal in which complainant also secured a share.
During this transaction complainant came in contact with end of Chandrakant (PO) namely Manoj Pawar who was working as a property dealer.
Complainant told him that he was looking for a flat for a reasonable amount.
Manoj had shown him a flat bearing no. 1253 Janta flat GTB Enclave in the year June 2005.

Manoj also introduced him to his neighbour's wife namely Rekha who was residing at house no. 1252 Janta Flat, GTB Enclave who told him that she could introduce him to the owner of the house namely Ved Prakash directly bypassing the property dealer for a reasonable amount.

On 28.06.2005, complainant was introduced to Ved Prakash the resident of F4/148, Sector 16, Rohini and the deal to purchase the abovesaid house was finalized for a sum of Rs. 5,40,000/-
and Rs. 15,000/- were given as earnest money were given to Ved Prakash at the house of Rekha in State vs Dharmendar Kr.

1 presence of Manoj, Chandrakant (PO), his wife Minakshi and friend of the wife of the complainant namely Seema.
The entire responsibilty was taken by Chandrakant (PO), Manoj and Rekha.
02. On that day, the registry of the flat was scheduled on 01.07.2005.
Accused Manoj and Chandrakant (PO) took the complainant in his car to F4/148, Sector 16, Rohini where he met Ved Prakash and his wife who was in a veil.
In presence of Manoj, Chandrakant (PO) Rs. 4,00,000/- in cash and a cheque bearing no. 508828 pertaining to ICICI BANK in sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- were given to Ved Prakash.
Ved Prakash told him that he was going to keep the amount to house of his brother in law.
Accused Manoj and Chandrakant (PO) also left.
Meanwhile, he realised that wife of Ved Prakash was also not there.
Complainant went downstairs and spoke to Manoj, Chandrakant (PO) and waited for Ved Prakash who did not Digitally signed by ISRA ISRA Date:

He called at 100 no. but Ved Prakash could not be found.

Thereafter, he realised that Rekha, Manoj and Chandrakant (PO) can conspired against him and the property documents of Flat No.
1253 which were given to him were fake.

It is alleged that Manoj, Chandrakant (PO),
Rekha and Ved Prakash cheated him for an amount of Rs. 4,15,000/-.

Hence, on the complaint of the complainant, an FIR against accused Jai Prakash @ Jagjeevan @
Ved Prakash (hereinafter, referred to as the accused persons) was registered under section 419/420/467/468/471/120-B/34 IPC.

A f t e r c o m p l e t i o n o f t h e i n v e s t i g a t i o n , c h a r g e - s h e e t u n d e r s e c t i o n s 419/420/467/468/471/120-B/34 IPC
was filed before the court against the accused persons.
The then Learned Magistrate took cognizance and accused was summoned to face the trial.
On his appearance in the Court, copies of documents, relied upon by the prosecution were supplied to him as per norms.

Thereafter, vide order dated 22.11.2025, charge under sections 420/34 IPC and 467/468/471/34 IPC was framed against accused Manoj, charge under section 420/34 IPC against accused Rekha and on 29.11.2025, change u/s. 420/34 IPC and 419 IPC was framed against accused Jai Prakash @ Jagjeevan @ Ved Prakash to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the matter was listed for PE.
FINAL ARGUMENTS 04.
The court heard final arguments on behalf of the both the parties on 06.12.2025.
Ld. Counsel for the accused submitted that the case against the accused is false and frivolous and has prayed that accused be acquitted of the offence charged.
Learned Substitute APP for the state submitted that accused be convicted of the offences under the above-mentioned sections as there is sufficient evidence on record to convict the accused.
This court has heard the submissions of Ld. Substitute APP for the State and Ld. Counsel for the accused.

The court has also diligently gone Digitally signed by ISRA ISRA Date:

BRIEF REASONS FOR THE JUST DECISION OF THE CASE 05.
At this stage, it is pertinent to throw some light on legal provisions.
In order to attract the ingredients of Section 419 IPC it is necessary that accused not only cheated the complainant but also impersonated himself.

It is pertinent to note that to ate an offence under section 420 IPC, there should not only be cheating, but as a consequence of cheating accused should have dishonestly induced the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy wholly or in part a valuable security and which is capable of being converted in a valuable security.
In order to attract Section 468 IPC, the prosecution must show that accused committed forgery for the purpose of cheating and used the forged document as genuine for the purpose of Section 471 IPC.
In the present case it is also to be shown that accused forged valuable security, will etc.
As far as section 120 (B) IPC is concerned the foundation criminal conspiracy is existence of an agreement between the accused persons.
06. Needless to mention, in criminal law, the burden of proof on the prosecution is that of beyond reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by adducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.

07. In the instant case, in order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution had to prove the following ingredients of the offences punishable u/s 419/420/467/468/471/34 IPC beyond reasonable doubt.

In the present case, PW1 Sh. Shyam Lal was summoned through DCP.
The process was received back with a report that no such person was found at the given address.
hereafter, vide order dated 29.11.2025, he was dropped from the list of witnesses.
Summons were also issued to PW Savita W/o Sh. Shyam Lal through DCP, which were received back with the same report that no such person was found on the given address.

Thereafter, vide order dated 06.12.2025,
he was dropped from the list of witnesses.
There is no other public witness, who was remained to be examined by the prosecution.
09. PE was closed as no fruitful purpose would have been served by examining the other witnesses.
Hence, continuation with the prosecution evidence would have been an exercise in futility.

Hence,
the opportunity to lead further prosecution evidence was closed.

Since there is nothing State vs Dharmendar Kr. @ Billu on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95945118/
3 incriminating which is on record against the accused persons, the statement of accused U/s 313 Cr.P.C. is dispensed with in the light of aforesaid legal position.

Reference may be made to a Division Bench judgment of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court passed in the case of Govind & Ors vs.
The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104(2003) DLT 510 wherein it was held that:-
"...In cases where ultimate chance of conviction is very bleak or there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction in such cases no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution and trial to continue.

Govind & Ors vs.
The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104(2003) DLT 510
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is advisable to truncate or snip the proceedings and save valuable time of the courts.
The trial should not be continued only for the purpose of formally completing the proceedings to pronounce the conclusion on a future date.........."

10. Since PW/complainant and his wife, who were material witnesses could not be examined as they could not be found at the given address even through DCP Digitally signed by ISRA ISRA Date:
ZAIDI ZAIDI 14:46:53 2025.12.06 +0800 concerned and they were dropped from the list of witnesses.
Nothing could come out on the record to prove the incident or the necessary ingredients of the offences as charged as there is no direct evidence to connect the accused persons with the crime.
11. The entire prosecution case hinged upon the statement of PW/complainant- star witness and his wife, who could not be examined.

Rest witnesses are formal in nature and the guilt of the accused cannot be established from their testimonies, in as much as, the alleged incident neither took place in their presence nor it is the case of the prosecution.

12. Therefore, keeping in view the overall conspectus of the case, this Court is of the considered view that the prosecution has miserably failed to discharge the burden imposed on it by law of satisfying this court beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the accused persons.
13. It is an adage that law works on the wheels of evidence.
Every criminal trial is a journey of discovering and unfolding the truth.
But in the present case no sufficient evidence is there on record to warrant the conviction of the accused person.

In the case of Prem Singh Yadav Vs. CBI 178 (2011)
DLT 529 it was held that where it is possible to have both views one in favor of prosecution and one in favor of accused, the later one should prevail.

entities.text:
Prem Singh Yadav Vs. CBI 178 (2011)
DLT 529
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The prosecution could not prove by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
In a criminal case the burden of proof is on the prosecution to prove the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The burden never shifts.
An accused enjoys the presumption of innocence.
There is no duty on an accused person to purge himself of guilt.
Where there is a lingering doubt, the accused person is given the benefit of the doubt.

14. For the reasons outlined above, this court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to discharge the heavy burden imposed on it by law of satisfying this court beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the accused persons.
